statements.justification: This is the published uniqueness theorem that converts the reconstructed complete conditional response into the Hawkes kernel.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 assumes the complete response is available and does not reconstruct it from two fixed-bin covariance lags.
statements.consumer: The broad stable nonzero recovery theorem uses precisely this uniqueness step after completing the response from the two observed lags.

statements.statement:
For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\), the nonsingular conditional-response density in \(\text{lem:bacry-muzy-wiener-hopf-uniqueness}\) agrees almost everywhere with \(g\) in \(\text{def:complete-hawkes-response}\).  Explicitly,
\[
 C_{+}(t)_{ij}=g^{ij}(t)\lambda_j\quad(t>0),
\]
and consequently
\[
 g(t)=C_{+}(t)D^{-1}\quad(t>0),\qquad
 g(t)=C_{+}(-t)^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}\quad(t<0).
\]
statements.justification: It audits the transpose and right-normalization needed to apply the published Wiener--Hopf theorem in this note's future-row covariance convention.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 writes the covariance with the earlier coordinate in the row, whereas this note writes the future coordinate in the row.
statements.consumer: The broad recovery theorem uses this bridge to pass its reconstructed covariance density to the cited conditional-response uniqueness theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\).  Equation (2) in the proof of \(\text{lem:stable-covariance-semigroup}\) gives \(\lambda_j>0\) for every \(j\), so conditioning on an infinitesimal type-\(j\) event is well normalized.  Let \(\bar g\) denote the nonsingular conditional-response density used in \(\text{lem:bacry-muzy-wiener-hopf-uniqueness}\).  For \(t>0\), there is no diagonal Dirac atom between times zero and \(t\).  Stationarity and \(\mathbb P\{dN_j(0)=1\}=\lambda_j\,dt+o(dt)\) therefore give, entry by entry,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_{+}(t)_{ij}\,dt^2
 &=\mathbb E\{dN_i(t)dN_j(0)\}-\lambda_i\lambda_j\,dt^2\\
 &=\lambda_j\,dt\left[
   \mathbb E\{dN_i(t)\mid dN_j(0)=1\}-\lambda_i\,dt
  \right]
 =\lambda_j\bar g^{ij}(t)\,dt^2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(C_{+}(t)=\bar g(t)D\), and right multiplication by \(D^{-1}\) is valid because \(D\succ0\).  Hence
\[
 \bar g(t)=C_{+}(t)D^{-1},\qquad t>0.
\tag{2}
\]
For \(t<0\), covariance symmetry and stationarity give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\{dN(t),dN(0)\}
 =C_{+}(-t)^{\mathsf T}\,dt^2.
\tag{3}
\]
Repeating (1) with the negative lag and retaining the time-zero coordinate in the conditioning column yields
\[
 \bar g(t)=C_{+}(-t)^{\mathsf T}D^{-1},\qquad t<0.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) are exactly the two branches in \(\text{def:complete-hawkes-response}\).  Values at \(t=0\) are irrelevant to the entrywise-\(L^1\) equivalence class and to convolution, proving the claim.

statements.statement:
For every \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:wiener-hopf-two-lag-inverse}\) is well defined, independent of the orthonormal basis \(O\), and independent of the admissible structural representative.  For every such representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\),
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\geq1,\quad S=\operatorname{im}(A),\quad
 F=[T|_S]_O,\quad L^{\mathrm{WH}}=[B|_S]_O,\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=[J|_S]_O^{-1},
\]
\[
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=K,\quad C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\quad(t>0),\quad
 D^{\mathrm{WH}}=D,\quad g^{\mathrm{WH}}=g,\quad
 \chi^{\mathrm{WH}}=\phi,
\]
\[
 M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=A/\beta,\quad M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=A/\beta^2,\quad
 u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}>0,\quad u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}>0,
\]
and
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Thus the mean and two positive fixed-bin covariance lags identify the entire stable nonzero common-exponential Hawkes mechanism, and hence its labeled graph, whenever the principal-log strip holds only on \(S=\operatorname{im}(A)\); no full-rank, zero-diagonal, coordinate-support, isolated-label, acyclicity, or invertible-active-block condition is required.  The regime is strictly broader than each such algebraic special case: for \(p=2\), every \(\Delta>0\), \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=\mathbf 1_2\), and \(A=\tfrac14\mathbf 1_2\mathbf 1_2^{\mathsf T}\) define an admissible member whose \(A\) is singular, self-exciting, reciprocal, and has the non-coordinate image \(\operatorname{span}(\mathbf 1_2)\).
statements.justification: It gives the broad population inverse requested by the directive, including singular, reciprocal, cyclic, and self-exciting stable mechanisms.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 identifies the kernel from the complete conditional response, whereas this theorem first reconstructs that entire response exactly from the mean and only two fixed-bin covariance lags.
statements.consumer: Coarsely timestamped multichannel alarm systems can be structurally identified beyond feed-forward graphs when the restricted principal-log strip is scientifically credible.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\) and choose an arbitrary admissible representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\).  By \(\text{def:stable-nonzero-restricted-strip-moment-image}\),
\[
 A\neq0,\quad
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\left.\Delta B\right|_{\operatorname{im}(A)}\right)
 \subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\}.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\text{lem:stable-covariance-semigroup}\),
\[
 S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{im}(A)=\operatorname{im}(K),\quad
 r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\geq1,\quad
 \Gamma_1=J^2K,\quad \Gamma_2=T\Gamma_1,
\tag{2}
\]
and \(B\) is Hurwitz, \(D\succ0\), and \(J\) is invertible.  The inequality \(r\geq1\) follows from \(A\neq0\).  Since \(A\operatorname{im}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{im}(A)\), the space \(S\) is invariant under \(A\), hence under \(B=A-\beta I_p\), \(T=e^{B\Delta}\), and \(J=\int_0^\Delta e^{Bu}\,du\).

Choose an admissible orthonormal basis \(O\) and put \(R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1\).  From (2), \(\Gamma_1=OR\).  Because both \(O\) and \(\Gamma_1\) have rank \(r\), \(R\) has full row rank, so \(RR^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).  There is a unique matrix \(F_0\) with \(TO=OF_0\).  Using \(\Gamma_2=T\Gamma_1\),
\[
 O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1}
 =F_0RR^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1}=F_0.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(F=F_0=[T|_S]_O\).  Put \(L_0=O^{\mathsf T}BO\); invariance gives \(BO=OL_0\), whence
\[
 F=e^{\Delta L_0}.
\tag{4}
\]
The restricted strip (1), (4), and \(\text{lem:principal-log-strip}\), applied in dimension \(r\), imply that the principal logarithm exists and
\[
 L^{\mathrm{WH}}=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F)=L_0=[B|_S]_O.
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(B|_S\) is Hurwitz, \(L^{\mathrm{WH}}\) is invertible, and every eigenvalue of \(F\) has modulus less than one; hence \(F-I_r\) is invertible.

Let \(J_S=O^{\mathsf T}JO\).  Integrating \(e^{Bu}O=Oe^{L_0u}\) and using (5) gives
\[
 J_S=\int_0^\Delta e^{L_0u}\,du
 =L_0^{-1}(F-I_r),\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=L^{\mathrm{WH}}(F-I_r)^{-1}=J_S^{-1}.
\tag{6}
\]
By (2), write \(K=OK_S\).  Since \(J^2O=OJ_S^2\), equations (2) and (6) yield
\[
 R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1=J_S^2K_S,\quad
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=O(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R
 =OJ_S^{-2}J_S^2K_S=K.
\tag{7}
\]
For \(t>0\), (5), (7), and \(\text{lem:stable-covariance-semigroup}\) therefore prove
\[
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)
 =Oe^{L^{\mathrm{WH}}t}(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R
 =e^{Bt}K=C_{+}(t).
\tag{8}
\]
This proves, using only \((\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), exact reconstruction of the entire positive-lag covariance density, not merely its values inside one bin.

Stationarity and the compensator identity give
\[
 m=\mathbb E\{N(\Delta)-N(0)\}
 =\mathbb E\int_0^\Delta\ell(u)\,du=\Delta\lambda.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(\Delta>0\), \(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}=m/\Delta=\lambda\), and hence \(D^{\mathrm{WH}}=D\succ0\).  Thus the inverse used in the definition of \(g^{\mathrm{WH}}\) exists.  For \(t>0\), the response orientation in \(\text{def:complete-hawkes-response}\) and (8) give
\[
 g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=C_{+}(t)D^{-1}=g(t).
\tag{10}
\]
For \(t<0\), stationarity gives
\(\operatorname{Cov}(dN(t),dN(0))=C_{+}(-t)^{\mathsf T}dt^2\); hence the second branch of the definition also equals \(g(t)\).  The chosen values at zero agree and are irrelevant to the convolution.  Therefore \(g^{\mathrm{WH}}=g\) almost everywhere on \(\mathbb R\).

The true kernel \(\phi(t)=Ae^{-\beta t}\mathbf 1_{\{t>0\}}\) is causal and entrywise integrable, and
\[
 \left(\int_0^\infty\phi^{ij}(t)\,dt\right)_{i,j}=A/\beta,\quad
 \rho(A/\beta)<1
\tag{11}
\]
by stable-class membership.  Therefore \(\text{lem:complete-response-orientation}\) and \(\text{lem:bacry-muzy-wiener-hopf-uniqueness}\), with the orientation verified in (10), say that \(\phi\) is the unique causal entrywise-\(L^1\) solution of the Wiener--Hopf equation driven by \(g^{\mathrm{WH}}\).  Existence and uniqueness of the defining operation follow, and
\[
 \chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=\phi(t)=Ae^{-\beta t}\mathbf 1_{\{t>0\}}.
\tag{12}
\]
This citation is used only for uniqueness from the already reconstructed complete response; it supplies no fixed-bin reconstruction step.

Since \(\beta>0\), entrywise integration of (12) gives
\[
 M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty Ae^{-\beta t}\,dt=A/\beta,\quad
 M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty tAe^{-\beta t}\,dt=A/\beta^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Put \(a_+=\mathbf 1_p^{\mathsf T}A\mathbf 1_p\).  Because \(A\geq0\) and \(A\neq0\), \(a_+>0\).  Hence
\[
 u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=a_+/\beta>0,\quad
 u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=a_+/\beta^2>0,\quad
 \beta^{\mathrm{WH}}=u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}/u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\beta,
\tag{14}
\]
so every division in the inverse is valid and
\[
 A^{\mathrm{WH}}=\beta^{\mathrm{WH}}M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=A.
\tag{15}
\]
Taking expectations in the intensity equation, as in the proof of \(\text{lem:stable-covariance-semigroup}\), gives
\[
 \lambda=\mu+(A/\beta)\lambda=\mu+M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}\lambda.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (9), (13), and (16) prove
\[
 \mu^{\mathrm{WH}}=(I_p-M_0^{\mathrm{WH}})\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}=\mu.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus the displayed recovery map returns the structural representative exactly.

For basis invariance, let \(O'=OU\) be another orthonormal basis of \(S\), where \(U\) is orthogonal.  Direct substitution and uniqueness of the principal logarithm give
\[
 R'=U^{\mathsf T}R,\quad F'=U^{\mathsf T}FU,\quad
 L^{\mathrm{WH}\prime}=U^{\mathsf T}L^{\mathrm{WH}}U,\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}\prime}=U^{\mathsf T}H^{\mathrm{WH}}U.
\tag{18}
\]
It follows that
\[
 O'e^{L^{\mathrm{WH}\prime}t}(H^{\mathrm{WH}\prime})^2R'
 =Oe^{L^{\mathrm{WH}}t}(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus \(K^{\mathrm{WH}}\), \(C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), \(g^{\mathrm{WH}}\), the unique \(\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}\), its moments, and the output do not depend on \(O\).  Every reconstructed quantity is consequently a function only of \(\eta\) and the known \(\Delta\).  Since the structural representative was arbitrary, (3)--(17) hold for every admissible representative and force all representatives to equal the same recovered triple.  Exact recovery of the labeled graph follows from \(G(A)=\{j\to i:A_{ij}>0\}\).

Finally, fix \(p=2\), \(\Delta>0\), \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=\mathbf 1_2\), and \(A=\tfrac14\mathbf 1_2\mathbf 1_2^{\mathsf T}\).  The eigenvalues of \(A\) are \(1/2\) and \(0\), so \(\rho(A/\beta)=1/2<1\), while \(A\geq0\), \(A\neq0\), and \(\mu>0\).  The standard immigration--birth construction is locally finite here directly: the expected number of generation-\(d\) descendants is governed by \((A/\beta)^d\), and \(\sum_{d\geq0}(A/\beta)^d=(I_2-A/\beta)^{-1}\) is finite entrywise.  Thus total cluster size has finite expectation and is finite almost surely; continuous exponential offspring delays give simplicity, and stationary Poisson immigration with rate \(\mu\) gives the stated Hawkes intensity.  Hence this triple induces a law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,2}^{\mathrm{stab}}\).  Its image is \(S=\operatorname{span}(\mathbf 1_2)\), and \(B|_S=-\tfrac12 I_S\), so the restricted spectrum is real and satisfies (1) for every \(\Delta>0\).  The matrix has determinant zero, both diagonal entries are positive, and both off-diagonal entries are positive.  Therefore it is simultaneously singular, self-exciting, reciprocal, and non-coordinate-image, as claimed.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\gamma\in\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\) and choose an arbitrary admissible representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\), with population mean \(m\).  By the two image definitions,
\[
 \eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}.
\tag{1}
\]
Apply \(\text{thm:stable-nonzero-two-lag-wiener-hopf-recovery}\) to (1).  Its proof through equations (2)--(8) uses only \((\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), not \(m\), to establish totality of the operations
\(r,S,O,R,F,L^{\mathrm{WH}},H^{\mathrm{WH}},K^{\mathrm{WH}}\) and to prove
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(A),\quad S=\operatorname{im}(A),\quad
 F=[T|_S]_O,\quad L^{\mathrm{WH}}=[B|_S]_O,\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=[J|_S]_O^{-1},\quad K^{\mathrm{WH}}=K,
\tag{2}
\]
\[
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=C_{+}(t),\qquad t>0.
\tag{3}
\]
The same theorem proves that (2)--(3) are basis invariant.

The curve in (3) extends continuously to zero, so the integral in \(\text{def:wiener-hopf-covariance-only-inverse}\) is finite.  Substituting (3) into \(\text{lem:zero-lag-bin-covariance}\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D^{\mathrm{WH},0}
 &=\Delta^{-1}\!\left[
 \Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)
 \{C_{+}(t)+C_{+}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt\right]\\
 &=D\succ0.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Therefore \(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH},0}=\operatorname{diag}(D)=\lambda\) and, using the mean identity in that lemma,
\[
 m^{\mathrm{WH},0}=\Delta\lambda=m.
\tag{5}
\]
The argument of \(\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\) in the covariance-only definition is consequently exactly the triple in (1).  The mean-plus-two-lag theorem now yields
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH},0}(\gamma)
 =\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)
 =(\beta,A,\mu).
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (2)--(6) show that every operation is defined.  Their left sides depend only on \(\gamma\), the known \(\Delta\), and an inessential basis; because the representative was arbitrary, they also prove representative independence and structural uniqueness.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate the raw mean and cross-moment vector \(\xi=\mathbb E[Y_0]\), apply \(\eta=\mathcal C(\xi)=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), select \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)\) by singular-value thresholding, and estimate the raw-moment long-run covariance \(\Omega(\theta)\) by a lag-window estimator. The single composite Jacobian \(\mathcal J(\theta)=D(\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\) produces both \(V(\theta)\) and the signed-edge covariance \(W(\theta)\). Uniform geometric mixing and the eighth-bin-count envelope are derived from finite-depth Poisson branching on the bounded fixed-margin class; the remaining inference restrictions are long-run covariance nonsingularity and the stated bandwidth condition. Support selection uses the separate vanishing threshold \(a_n\), while fixed-level Gaussian-maximum inversion is used only for conservative simultaneous-coordinate and graph-inclusion coverage.

tldr: Coarse timestamping need not erase Hawkes direction when a labeled feed-forward network is acyclic and all edges share one unknown exponential decay. Acyclicity is the contribution-defining scientific restriction: self-loops are allowed by the graph convention and therefore excluded as cycles of length one, rather than by a separate zero-diagonal assumption. The core claim is that the stationary mean and exactly two positive fixed-bin covariance matrices determine the active image \(\operatorname{im}(A)\), the decay through the restricted transition, the finite nilpotent logarithm, every directed amplitude through an antisymmetric covariance jump, and the baselines.
